headline: The K_p* conclusion INVERTED. Error grows monotonically with gain in BOTH damping groups; a higher gain buys no noise robustness.
v41_claim_retired: v4.1 said K_p* = 200 stays competitive at 18.6% because faster transients improve per-roller noise averaging. Under the weighted estimator that noise-averaging benefit does not appear.

campaign_condition.note: This is the tension-only gain-sweep campaign condition, NOT the representative dual-channel condition of Table 1 and Fig. 3 where E_Toggle reads 42.6%. The matching 50 Hz data were not rerun.
campaign_condition.grid: 10 plants x 2 K_p levels {50, 200} x (1 NF + 3 SN seeds)
campaign_condition.seed_structure: K_p* = 50 and 200 pool three seeds per plant; the K_p* = 100 cell is the matching single-seed slice of the factorial sweep.

damping_groups.definition: zeta_CL,min is the smallest damping ratio among the eigenmodes of the closed-loop A matrix at the nominal cascade gains.
damping_groups.pooling: The gain analysis pools H-Osc with O-UD, giving an 8:2 split.

simpsons_paradox.explanation: The pooled median's shallow minimum at K_p* = 100 is a Simpson's-paradox composition artifact of the imbalanced 8:2 group mix. NEITHER group shares it. Do not read '100 is best' as an accuracy result.

default_gain_rationale.kept_for: identifiability and safety, not noise averaging
default_gain_rationale.note: K_p* = 100 preserves the EA estimate that the highest gains destroy.

P08.note: The penalty of the highest gain falls on the stiffest, fastest plant, not the most flexible web. Plotted as a clipped off-scale triangle at K_p* = 200.

noise_free_gain_sweep.value_status: approximate endpoints only; no per-gain table is published
noise_free_gain_sweep.note: The ten-plant median error also grows steadily with gain under noise-free logs.

ET1_at_default_gain.condition: tension-only sensor noise at 0.3% of T_max, LPF 100 Hz, Tlog = 20 ms
ET1_at_default_gain.note: The K_p* sweep was run with E_Toggle; this is the ET1 value at the default K_p* = 100. ET1 itself was not swept over gain. Recomputed from a v4-era 31.4% figure.

overshoot.note: The gain sweep logs no transient metric, so the overshoot cost of an off-default gain is NOT quantified. A set of overshoot numbers that had no traceable source was deleted from v4.1.

retuned_optimum.note: The retuned optimum sits near K_p* ~ 15, so a warm start seeded at the SysID-mode K_p* = 100 is roughly seven times too stiff.

recommendation: K_p* = 100 remains the default, chosen for identifiability and safety. A higher gain buys no noise robustness: error grows monotonically with gain in both damping groups.
notes: The Kp* = 100 group values are not absent from the paper: Fig. 6 plots all three gains as grouped bars. Previously null with a 'do not synthesize' note; now filled from the figure package. The 50 and 200 values there match the printed ones exactly.
